deckName: KS3 DT · J1 Lesson 1 — Mission Control (Teacher Deck)

slides.kicker: OUR LADY'S GRAMMAR SCHOOL · DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY
slides.heading: Lesson 1 · Mission Control
slides.sub: Your first Digital Technology lesson — Year 8 · Lesson 1 of 17
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: sitting down, logged in to the computer, nothing else open.

SAY: welcome them in properly. Names, smiles, no screens yet — the lesson starts with you, not the computers.

WHEN TO MOVE: as soon as the room is settled.

slides.heading: In this lesson you will…
bullets: Log in with your own account — and learn how to keep it safe.
Learn the rules of the DT rooms.
Find your way around the lesson website, and earn your first badges.
Show what you already know — nothing today is a test.
Choose the codename that will be yours all year.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: still eyes front.

SAY: read the five lines out. Tell them the fourth one matters — nothing today is a test, and nobody can fail anything.

WHEN TO MOVE: straight on.

slides.heading: What today is
bullets: Your very first Digital Technology lesson at Our Lady's.
Today gets you set up for the whole year: log in, find your way around, and know where your work is saved.
You will earn your first badges as you go — and finish with a codename of your own.
slides.notes:
SAY: set the tone — calm and unhurried, everyone gets there.

WHEN TO MOVE: straight on.

slides.heading: The rules of this room
bullets: Food and drink stay packed away — one spill can end a computer.
Line up quietly outside until your teacher arrives.
Something broken, stuck or strange on screen? Tell your teacher straight away — you are never in trouble for reporting.
Sit properly, and give your eyes regular breaks from the screen.
Your login is YOURS: never share it, and sign out every time.
Before you leave: chair in, area tidy, signed out.
slides.notes:
SAY: deliver these as OUR rules, not the website's. The website revisits them later in the hour — you are giving the answers first, on purpose.

WHEN TO MOVE: straight on.

slides.heading: How the lessons work
bullets: Everything lives on one screen called Mission Control — seventeen lessons on one board, all year.
The main parts of each lesson are named sections called badges. Finish one, earn its badge.
Badges bring points called XP. XP unlocks new colours for the website later in the year — it is private to you and your teacher, and nobody is ranked.
Click an answer and you find out straight away whether you were right — and why. Read the reason every time.
Stuck? The round ? button is on every screen — and your teacher is always the last step.
slides.notes:
SAY: point at the picture on the right — this is what every marked answer looks like: the verdict, the reason, then Next. Tell them to read the reason every single time, because that is where the learning is.

If the connection to the website slows down, a clicked answer says Checking… for a few seconds instead of answering straight away — worth one calm sentence if it happens.

WHEN TO MOVE: straight on.

slides.heading: One screen to get past — watch first
bullets: The first time you open our class website, Google checks you are happy to let it in.
You will see the next four screens ONCE — and never again.
Watch the board first. Then we all do it together.
slides.notes:
SAY: talk through the four pictures before anyone touches a mouse. Then walk the room while they do it.

WHEN TO MOVE: straight on to the four steps.

slides.heading: Step 1 · It says Unverified — that is expected
slides.text:
This website was built specially for our school, and Google says this about anything a school builds for itself.

Press REVIEW PERMISSIONS.
slides.notes: SAY: the word Unverified frightens people. Normalise it before anyone meets it alone.

slides.heading: Step 2 · What Google will share
slides.text:
Just your name and your school email — so the website knows who you are.

Press Continue.
slides.notes: The navy bars in the picture are where each pupil's own name and school email appear.

slides.heading: Step 3 · Tick Select all
slides.text:
These ticks let the website do its lesson jobs with your school account — like checking the folders you build in your own Drive later.

Tick the Select all box — all three ticks appear together.
slides.notes: Ticking the three boxes one at a time works too. If anyone asks what the ticks mean: they let the lesson website work with the pupil's school Google account — for example the side quest checks the folders they build in their own Drive.

slides.heading: Step 4 · Scroll down, press Continue
slides.text: That is it — you will never see these screens again.
slides.notes: Anyone stuck here has usually missed the scroll: the Continue button hides below the fold.

slides.heading: Ready? Go.
bullets: Open Google Classroom — the class link is waiting there.
Bookmark it: press the star, save to the Bookmarks bar.
Read the Welcome together, then work to the END OF BADGE 2 — and stop there.
Your screen tells you everything else. Stuck? The round ? button, then a hand up.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: about to touch their screens for the first time.

SAY: the Welcome screen is worth reading ALOUD together — it types itself out, so wait for the last line, then read it while they follow on their own screens.

Then they work alone: warm-up, Badge 1, Badge 2. Say the stop rule now — "when you finish Badge 2, stop and look up."

Walk the room. Quietly hand a credential slip to anyone whose login will not work.

WHEN TO MOVE: when the first pupils finish Badge 2, stop the whole room for the Vault.

slides.heading: STOP — eyes front · The Vault
bullets: You are about to be PAIRED with someone in this class — the website chooses, and it will tell you who.
You share one Vault between two screens and take turns at the controls.
Agree in the chat BEFORE a file moves — and say why: "it goes there because…"
If the Vault throws a file back, you were wrong — talk it out and go again.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: they have just finished Badge 2. Screens ignored, eyes front.

SAY: "You are about to be paired with someone in this class — the website chooses, and they are probably not beside you. You share one Vault between two screens and take turns. Agree in the chat BEFORE a file moves. If the Vault throws a file back, you were wrong — talk it out and go again."

Point at each picture in turn: the door they will read, the waiting card while a partner is found, and the pop-up that names their partner. Naming these now is what stops thirty hands going up.

THEN send them in. On your own screen open the Live tab — the pairing panel shows who is waiting and who is paired; press Solo run beside anyone left stranded.

Expect the room to get noisy. That is the activity working.

WHEN TO MOVE: when most Vaults are sealed, stop the room again.

slides.heading: The Real Vault
bullets: The Vault you just filed was pretend — the real one is called Google Drive.
Yours follows YOUR login: any computer in school, and at home tonight.
Find the + New button — a side quest after this lesson builds your folders there.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: Vaults sealed, still facing front.

DO: show YOUR own Drive on the board — drive.google.com, and the + New button.

SAY: "The Vault you just filed was pretend — this is the real one. Yours follows YOUR login: any computer in the school, and at home tonight."

Then let them find theirs and tick the steps.

WHEN TO MOVE: two or three minutes, no more.

slides.heading: STOP — The Licence Exam
bullets: You will answer sixteen quick questions on your own, in silence.
It is NOT a test: you cannot fail it, and nobody marks it.
It is a photograph of what you know TODAY — in June you will see how far you have come.
The screen says "Answer saved" and nothing else. That is it working.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: back from the Real Vault, facing front.

SAY, before they touch it: "Quiet and on your own now. It is not a test: you cannot fail it, and I am not marking it. It is a photograph of what you know today — in June we will look at it again and you will see how far you have come. The screen says Answer saved and nothing else. That is it working."

Point at the second picture as you say the last line — it is the one that worries them.

The room now goes quiet for about fifteen minutes. If someone says it is not marking, one calm reminder to the class settles it.

Nothing for you to mark afterwards: scores land in the Live tab's Baseline column.

WHEN TO MOVE: when the room has finished.

slides.heading: STOP — Your Codename
bullets: Shuffle as often as you like until you find a name you love.
Once you press and hold to sign, the name is yours for the WHOLE YEAR.
Then sign the five promises — read them properly, they are real.
Give the last message thirty seconds of quiet — it is about you.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: exam finished, facing front.

SAY: let it be fun, but give two warnings first. "Shuffle as often as you like — but once you hold that button down and sign, the name is yours for the whole year." And the signing is press-and-hold, so nobody signs by accident.

Give the closing message thirty seconds of quiet — it tells them that finding this hard at first is normal, and that they belong here. It is the best thirty seconds of the hour.

WHEN TO MOVE: when the room has signed.

slides.heading: The last two screens
bullets: One final question — this one IS marked, so think.
Then "How did it go?" — three honest ratings and a private comment.
The comment box comes to your teacher and nobody else.
Everyone finishes both screens before leaving.
slides.notes:
SAY: "Last question — this one is marked, so think. Then tell me honestly how today felt. The comment box comes to me and nobody else."

Nobody leaves without finishing How did it go? It is how you hear from the pupils who never put a hand up.

WHEN TO MOVE: when both screens are done.

slides.heading: Before you leave
bullets: Sign out properly — if you stay signed in, the next person at this machine IS you.
Chairs in, area tidy.
Next lesson you make a computer react.
slides.notes:
SAY: hold the room to the two rules the lesson just taught — sign out, tidy up. "If you stay signed in, the next person at this machine IS you as far as the school is concerned."

Then tell them what is coming: next lesson they make a real computer react to a button press.
